---
title: "Scatter plots"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
```

A scatter uses the small dot, `data-primary` at 70% opacity with no edge,
which keeps a dense cloud readable. Both axes carry gridlines and, as the
only chart family where the axes need naming, both carry titles.

## Dots

```{r dots}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_gla_dot(size = 2.5) +
  gla_labs(
    title = "Heavier cars use more fuel", subtitle = "Weight against fuel economy, 32 cars from 1974",
    source = "Motor Trend, 1974", x = "Weight (1,000 lb)", y = "Miles per gallon"
  ) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "both", axis_titles = "both")
```

## Coloured by a series

```{r series}
cars <- transform(mtcars, cyl = paste(cyl, "cylinders"))
ggplot(cars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = cyl)) +
  geom_gla_dot(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_gla() +
  gla_labs(
    title = "The heaviest cars have eight cylinders", subtitle = "Weight against fuel economy",
    source = "Motor Trend, 1974", x = "Weight (1,000 lb)", y = "Miles per gallon"
  ) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "both", axis_titles = "both")
```

## Faceted

```{r faceted, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(cars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_gla_dot(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(cyl)) +
  gla_labs(title = "Weight against fuel economy, by cylinders", x = "Weight (1,000 lb)", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "both", axis_titles = "both")
```

## Picking out a point

`geom_gla_marker()` is the larger hollow marker. With `stat_gla_end()` it
picks the high, the low or the ends of a series.

```{r marker}
ggplot(gla_yearly, aes(year, average, colour = series)) +
  geom_gla_line() +
  stat_gla_end(where = "max", geom = GeomGlaMarker, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2024) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_gla() +
  gla_labs(title = "Each variable's peak year", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP)", x = NULL) +
  theme_gla()
```

## Interactive

`gla_plotly()` turns the finished chart into an interactive one through
plotly. A scatter plot converts with its dots, and a faceted one keeps its
panels with the strips at the left of each.

```{r interactive, eval = requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)}
gla_plotly(last_plot())
```
